nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: Edmund. Good God, man. Sit down. I heard this morning — I came as soon as I could.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: Clara was — she was a remarkable woman. I want you to know that everyone here feels this deeply.

nodes.speaker: Edmund
nodes.text: It wasn't the Ripper, Arthur. The police closed it in minutes but something doesn't fit.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: I understand the mind reaches for anything rather than accept the randomness of it. I've seen it before. With other families.

nodes.speaker: Edmund
nodes.text: I set type on every Ripper story we've run. Every detail. The position of the body was wrong, Arthur. The wounds don't match the pattern.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: Then you should look into it. I mean that. If you're right — that's a story, Edmund. That's important.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: Take as much time as you need away from the press. Your position is safe. I'll see to the children if you need.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: There was a story — unverified, I couldn't run it — about Councillor Hargrove and his Whitmore Street properties. Clara might have crossed paths with that world through her charity work.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: It's probably nothing. But if she'd got involved in something involving Hargrove — that's a dangerous man.
nodes.journal_entry: Arthur pointed me toward Hargrove. He seemed genuinely shaken by Clara's death. He's known me fifteen years.
